messages:
jess: FYI Mistral is seeing auth-related backpressure on their dedicated pool (mistral-prod-eu). Started ~10:12 UTC, intermittent 429s and long-tail latency. @linh tagging you for AM touch.

maria: customer reports baseline QPS ~220, spikes to 650 for ~3–6m windows. Their app retries aggressively which worsens queueing.

linh: noted. Account says they purchased 6 GPUs but average utilization is low except during spikes. wants guidance on headroom and warmup.

omar: digging into serving logs — seeing repeated token-check timeouts followed by immediate 429s; runtime indicates inflight cap hit then gateway gating. Sample from runtime log: 

```
2026-02-14T10:12:35Z SERVE [pool=mistral-prod-eu] inflight=792 cap=800 backpressure=true route=gateway-01
2026-02-14T10:12:35Z AUTH timeout uid=0x7f2a tokencheck=1500ms -> 429
```

omar: autoscaler didn't spin up quick enough. Current autoscale policy uses "p95_latency" threshold and min_replicas=3, max=12, scale_cooldown=120s. For short bursts p95 triggers late.

elena: that explains slow reaction — p95 is noisy for these 3–6m bursts. We should switch to using short-window avg inflight or request_rate metric for scaling decisions. Also the customer's model variants have uneven cost per token; noisy tenant probably consuming disproportionate GPU time.

sre-bot: alert -> pool:mistral-prod-eu util=96% (10:14:12), enqueue=230, 429_rate=11%

mistral-cust: we're seeing a lot of 429s around 10:12-10:20. Some requests succeed later, but clients interpret 429 as fatal. This hurts UX. What can we do immediately?

jess: short-term mitigation: 1) increase min_replicas to 5 for next 48h, 2) enable short warmup ramp (pre-spin for scheduled traffic windows), 3) apply request-level retry headers to be more conservative (client side). I'll propose a transient config change.

elena: medium-term: change autoscale trigger to use `sum(inflight)` over 30s window and a target of 70% GPU utilization; reduce scale_cooldown to 30s for bursty customers. Add a per-tenant concurrency cap to prevent noisy neighbor thrash.

omar: repro steps I used: 

```
# spike generator (10m run, ramp to 700 qps)
wrk -t8 -c700 -d00:10:00 --latency \ \
  -s ./post.lua --  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

omar: with that load the pool inflight hits cap and auth requests pile up, token-check backend (customer side) has occasional 1.5s cold JWT verifications causing cascading 429s. So two contributors: pool sizing + external auth latency.

mistral-cust: auth backend is a third-party we can't change quickly. Can you add more headroom on our end?

maria: immediate plan: bump min_replicas to 5, set an emergency headroom of +30% burst capacity, and apply a per-tenant soft concurrency limit of 120 inflight. This should reduce 429s during retries.

elena: ops note — we should also set a fallback model routing to a cheaper, lower-latency variant for requests that exceed a 500ms auth threshold so user requests don't all fail. We'll coordinate with runtime to add a routing policy with fallback=true for Mistral.

linh: communicated to customer: we'll apply transient capacity changes in next 10m and monitor. Also recommend they stagger retries and add jitter.

omar: follow-up engineering actions assigned: 
- @elena (eng-runtime): change autoscale metric to sum(inflight)_30s and reduce cooldown to 30s for pool overrides.
- @omar (oncall-sre): apply min_replicas=5 and tenant concurrency cap now, roll back after 48h if stable.
- @jess (support): coordinate with customer for warmup windows and confirm whether usage has predictable bursts.

sre-bot: deployment started -> change-set id=chg-20260214-58 (min_replicas, concurrency-cap). Monitor channel for regression.

mistral-cust: thanks, we're standing by. We'll suppress aggressive client retries until you confirm.

jess: post-mortem notes to collect: list of external auth latencies, per-tenant qps during spikes, model variant token-cost distribution, and timeline of autoscale signals. Owner: jess. ETA: 48h.

elena: also scheduling a shortplaybook for sales/CS to recommend reserved headroom for customers with unpredictable third-party auth. Template will include recommended min_replicas, concurrency limits, and warmup scripts.

maria: closing loop: will send customer update + metrics dashboard link once deployment stabilizes. :thumbsup:
